Title: Checkout snapshot — create_checkout totals agree with the cart it was composed from
Preconditions: vcst-qa on the build pinned in this suite's manifest notes (config/test-suites.json, suite 102) — UCP 3.1006.0-pr-7-612c / Platform 3.1072.0-pr-3108-b6ef / storefront 2.59.0-pr-2467-1951. MCP endpoint {{FRONT_URL}}/ucp/mcp — STOREFRONT host only (Platform host cannot mint a matching-audience token; see suite notes). Token recipe, ambient REST context and the SEARCH_TERM rule are in the suite notes — do not restate them per case. Role: @td(ACME_ADMIN.email). THE CART IS CLEARED FIRST and cleared again on teardown. Two reasons, both measured 2026-09-23: create_cart UPSERTS into the authenticated buyer's existing default cart rather than opening a fresh one (proved by UCPA-028), so without the clear this case reads a cart nobody in this suite composed — observed total 1203699 against an arithmetic expectation of 88700, and the P1 line climbing 8 -> 14 -> 16 across consecutive runs of this very case, i.e. the case was polluting a SHARED fixture account every time it ran. The reset is done with update_cart, not create_cart: create_cart UPSERTS (it raises the quantity of a line already present), whereas update_cart takes the COMPLETE DESIRED STATE of the named cart, so passing exactly one line at quantity 2 makes the cart exactly that regardless of what it held before. Two steps are needed because update_cart requires cart_id (400 invalid_request without it) and no tool returns the default cart id on its own, while create_cart refuses an empty line_items[] (400, "line_items must contain at least one item") — so the bootstrap create_cart resolves the buyer to their one cart and yields its id, and the update_cart that follows sets the state this case asserts on. SINGLE LINE, not two: the second product this case used to add ({{TERM2}}'s SKU) carries a minimum order quantity of 2 and has under 2 in stock on vcst-qa, so create_cart drops the line with a recoverable PRODUCT_MIN_QTY_NOT_AVAILABLE and reports ucp.status success anyway (the same silent-drop shape UCPA-025 owns) — an unconstrained live-discover of "the first two products" is exactly the fixture the SECOND RULE warns about, because it is not constrained on orderability, the one dimension this case is sensitive to. Cleanup deliberately omits logout_buyer: this role is a shared fixture also used by other suites, and logout_buyer revokes ALL of a buyer's Platform OAuth sessions ("including other sessions," per its own tool description).

[GQL-EXEC discover1]
[GQL-CAPTURE discover1.data.products.items.0.code → TERM1]
[MCP-OP search1]
search_products
{ "store_id": "{{STORE_ID}}", "query": "{{TERM1}}", "limit": 1 }

[MCP-CAPTURE search1.products.0.id → P1_ID]

Title: NET-NEW — stock enforcement is per REQUESTED LINE ENTRY, not per consolidated cart total: splitting the same over-stock quantity across two line entries (or two sequential calls) for the same product bypasses the hard refusal entirely
Preconditions: vcst-qa on the build pinned in this suite's manifest notes (config/test-suites.json, suite 102) — UCP 3.1006.0-pr-7-612c / Platform 3.1072.0-pr-3108-b6ef / storefront 2.59.0-pr-2467-1951. MCP endpoint {{FRONT_URL}}/ucp/mcp — STOREFRONT host only (Platform host cannot mint a matching-audience token; see suite notes). Token recipe, ambient REST context and the SEARCH_TERM rule are in the suite notes — do not restate them per case. Fixture: @td(PROD_LOW_STOCK.sku). Anonymous cart. Verified live 2026-09-23, twice independently: (a) ONE create_cart call with TWO line_items entries for the SAME product_id whose quantities sum to captured+1, and (b) TWO SEQUENTIAL create_cart calls passing the same buyer_id (the documented upsert-add semantics, BL-CART-007 / UCPA-028) that raise the SAME line to captured+1 — BOTH land on a DIFFERENT, softer code path than UCPA-032's single untouched line entry: the line is CREATED/RAISED to the over-stock quantity, the top-level envelope AND cart-level messages[] stay EMPTY, and the only signal is a LINE-level PRODUCT_QTY_CHANGED message with severity=recoverable. This is the exact operation-level-vs-line-level split the runner doc already documents for xCart (graphql-test-cases-runner.md §4.1) — UCP inherits it. Framed as OBSERVED, not asserted-wrong: no documented spec says composition must be rejected identically to a single over-limit entry, and BL-CART-002 is cited as the AT-RISK invariant this composition path could undermine at checkout, not as a confirmed violation (checkout-time enforcement of this line's isValid state is out of this case's scope — see Failure_Signals).
Steps:
[MCP-OP search1]
search_products
{ "store_id": "{{STORE_ID}}", "query": "{{sku}}", "limit": 5 }
[MCP-EXEC search1]
[MCP-CAPTURE search1.products.0.id → PRODUCT_ID]
[MCP-CAPTURE search1.products.0.availability.available_quantity → AVAILABLE_QTY]
[MCP-OP cart1]
create_cart
{ "store_id": "{{STORE_ID}}", "line_items": [{ "product_id": "{{PRODUCT_ID}}", "quantity": {{AVAILABLE_QTY}} }, { "product_id": "{{PRODUCT_ID}}", "quantity": 1 }] }
[MCP-EXEC cart1]
Assertions:
[ERRORS label=cart1] HTTP 200 {OBSERVED}
[DATA label=cart1] body.ucp.status = success {OBSERVED}
[COUNT label=cart1] body.cart.line_items.length = 1 {OBSERVED} -- consolidated into ONE line, not refused, not left as two
[DATA label=cart1] body.cart.line_items.0.quantity = {{AVAILABLE_QTY}} + 1 {OBSERVED} -- the persisted quantity genuinely EXCEEDS available stock
[COUNT label=cart1] body.cart.line_items.0.messages[*?code=PRODUCT_QTY_CHANGED].length > 0 {OBSERVED} -- the ONLY signal this happened, and it lives on the LINE's own messages[], one level deeper than UCPA-032's cart/top-level signal
[COUNT label=cart1] body.cart.messages.length = 0 {OBSERVED} -- cart-level messages stay empty
[COUNT label=cart1] body.messages.length = 0 {OBSERVED} -- top-level messages stay empty too — UCPA-032's operation-level signal is ABSENT on this path
Cross_Layer_Checks: [EVIDENCE] whether this line's over-stock quantity actually blocks Place Order at checkout (BL-CART-002's own enforcement point) is NOT covered by this case or anywhere else in this suite — checkout_and_handoff's own status is a hardcoded 'requires_escalation'/'incomplete' constant per the domain map (D-checkout-status), not a computed validity check, so this is a genuine coverage gap worth a dedicated case once a reachable checkout-completion path exists on the machine lane
Failure_Signals: line_items.0.messages[] reverting to empty with no signal at all (silent overselling with NO warning anywhere, worse than today); the top-level or cart-level messages[] gaining PRODUCT_FFC_QTY here too (behavior converging with UCPA-032 — re-verify as a product change, not a regression, before filing)
